articles.title: Joe Milton Joins Cowboys Practice Squad After QB Goes Unclaimed on Waivers
articles.summary: Although the Dallas Cowboys waived quarterback Joe Milton, he is remaining with the organization after signing with the practice squad.
articles.body:
Although the Dallas Cowboys waived quarterback Joe Milton, he is remaining with the organization after signing with the practice squad.

Both COO/co-owner Stephen Jones and head coach Brian Schottenheimer had expressed significant interest in having the signal-caller back in the mix via the practice squad after his release earlier in the week.

Jones made his remarks on the DLLS Cowboys podcast, and Schottenheimer revealed his feelings to reporters during his Tuesday press conference.

The Cowboys were fortunate to get that chance to bring him back after Milton went unclaimed on waivers.

Milton initially made the 53-man roster after cuts were announced on Sunday. However, Dallas changed course after claiming running back Emari Demercado off waivers from the Kansas City Chiefs on Monday.

The Cowboys started with three quarterbacks on the 53-man roster in starter Dak Prescott, Milton and Sam Howell, although it was unclear who the Cowboys would choose to be Prescott's backup.

Schottenheimer had this to say on the matter Monday, per ESPN's Todd Archer , after the Demercado signing became official (and before Milton was let go).

"We're still piecing the puzzle together, and that's where this thing is very fluid," Schottenheimer said.

The Cowboys ultimately chose Howell as their QB2, making a switch from 2025, when Milton was Prescott's backup. Schottenheimer explained why.

"I think when we looked at the whole body of work, we just felt like Sam had done a little bit more in terms of executing the offense in certain areas," Schottenheimer told reporters on Tuesday, per DallasCowboys.com Staff Writer Tommy Yarrish .

"To have Joe Milton back would be incredible, we'll see what happens with the claims, and then see what he wants to do. We've shown that we know how to develop him. I think him being in this system for another year would be amazing, but I also know that he should have choices. And so, we'll see what happens, but in terms of wanting [Milton] back, absolutely."

Schottenheimer also said it was a "very, very hard decision" en route to choosing Howell, who signed a one-year deal with Dallas this offseason.

Milton did quite well this preseason, completing 29-of-43 passes (67.4 percent) for 378 yards and three touchdowns. Howell impressed as well, going 27-of-40 (67.5 percent) for 314 yards, three touchdowns and one interception.

Howell won the battle, but Milton could still be a part of the team's future.

Dallas opens the regular season on Sunday, Sept. 13 at the New York Giants.

articles.title: Lamar Jackson Contract Extension Talks Updated By Ravens GM Ahead of 2026 NFL Season
articles.summary: Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson's five-year, $260 million contract expires after the 2027 season, but general manager Eric DeCosta expressed optimism that the team can get an extension done with the two-time NFL MVP by March during a chat with reporters on Wednesday.
articles.body:
Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson's five-year, $260 million contract expires after the 2027 season, but general manager Eric DeCosta expressed optimism that the team can get an extension done with the two-time NFL MVP by March during a chat with reporters on Wednesday.

Jackson, who is entering his ninth season with the Ravens, is a four-time Pro Bowler and three-time First Team All-Pro who has led Baltimore to the playoffs in six of his campaigns.

Jackson's 8.3 adjusted passing yards per attempt and 102.2 quarterback rating stand first all-time in NFL history, per Pro Football Reference . He's also led the Ravens to a 76-31 record in his starts. Needless to say, it behooves the Ravens to keep the 29-year-old Jackson aboard long-term.

Last year was a tougher campaign for Jackson, who suffered multiple injuries, missed four games and saw his production dip after a 2024 season that ended with him finishing second in the NFL MVP race. Jackson told reporters in August that injuries in particular limited his mobility.

He goes into this season healthy, though, and that represents a chance Jackson can return to his usual form as a game-breaking dual threat.

If so, one can surmise his value would only go up. It's unclear what kind of contract Jackson, who is his own agent, would covet. At the top of the QB market , though, sits Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes and his $448 million deal ($64 million average per year).

Cleveland Browns quarterback Deshaun Watson leads the NFL in total guarantees ($230 million) on his fully guaranteed five-year deal that ends after this season, though one can surmise that's something we may never see for a long time after the contract backfired on the team due to his poor performance.

Otherwise, Buffalo Bills quarterback Josh Allen's $147 million guaranteed leads the way.

Negotiations between Jackson and the Ravens got ugly in March 2023, when Baltimore placed a non-exclusive franchise tag on the quarterback and Jackson requested a trade after saying "the team has not been interested in meeting my value." However, the two sides eventually came together for his current five-year deal, signed in April 2023.

The guess here, based on DeCosta's remarks, is that these negotiations could go smoother than the last time around. In the meantime, the Ravens are getting ready for Week 1 at the Indianapolis Colts on Sept. 13.

articles.title: Disgraced former Ravens kicker Justin Tucker reportedly works out for Jets
articles.summary: Tucker hasn't kicked in an NFL game since his release by the Ravens in 2025 after 16 women accused him of sexual misconduct.
articles.body:
Former Baltimore Ravens kicker Justin Tucker worked out for the New York Jets on Wednesday, according to multiple reports . Tucker was part of a group workout that also featured Michael Badgley and Josh Karty, NFL insider Jordan Schultz reports .

The Jets are in search of a kicker after Jason Sanders missed an extra point and a 54-yard field-goal attempt in Friday's preseason loss to the Giants, concluding a failed competition for the job from training camp. The Jets have since waived Sanders and claimed Blake Grupe off waivers. Sanders is back with the team on the practice squad.

Tucker was an eight-time Pro Bowler and five-time first-team All-Pro for the Baltimore Ravens in 13 seasons with the team. The Ravens released Tucker in 2025 after 16 women accused him of sexual misconduct that he allegedly engaged in repeatedly over the course of years during massage therapy sessions.

Tucker has denied the allegations and was not criminally charged.

Weeks after the Ravens cut Tucker, the NFL announced he was suspended for 10 games for violating the league's personal conduct policy. Tucker has not kicked in an NFL game since.

The Saints and Colts both reportedly worked Tucker out over the summer, but he did not make either roster. With New York's kicker position still unsettled, the Jets are giving Tucker a shot.

Tucker was one of the most accurate and reliable kickers in NFL history during his tenure with the Ravens. But his performance declined in his final season with the team prior to the news of the scandal and his release. He converted a career-low 73.3% of his field-goal attempts in 2024, well below his career conversion rate of 89.1%.

articles.title: Super Bowl-winning coach Charlie ‘Kippy’ Brown, Memphis’ first Black quarterback, dead at 71
articles.summary: Super Bowl-winning coach, the first Black quarterback in Memphis history, Charlie "Kippy" Brown dead at 71 years old. Pete Carroll called him a "great friend."
articles.body: Super Bowl-winning coach Charles "Kippy" Brown died this week at age 71. His cause of death is unknown. Brown began his football career as a quarterback at the University of Memphis from 1974-77, becoming the first Black quarterback in school history. The school inducted Brown into the M Club Hall of Fame in 2016 and he was inducted into the Tennessee Sports Hall of Fame in 2019. He also was honored with the Billy J. Murphy Award. CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE The Sweetwater, Tennessee, native then began his coaching career at his alma mater in 1978. After spending time at Louisville and Tennessee as a wide receivers coach, Brown transitioned to the pro ranks. With the New York Jets he was the team’s running backs coach from 1990-92. He returned to Tennessee for two years to be the team's wide receivers coach after his Jets tenure. Brown then returned to the pro level for the rest of his career, except for one year in 2009 when he went back to Tennessee to be a wide receivers coach. Brown coached for the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, Miami Dolphins, Green Bay Packers, Houston Texans, Detroit Lions and Seattle Seahawks. He spent one year as the head coach of the Memphis Maniax of the XFL. ZERO BS. JUST DAKICH. TAKE THE DON'T @ ME PODCAST ON THE ROAD. DOWNLOAD NOW! He was the Seahawks' wide receivers coach from 2010-14 when they made consecutive Super Bowl runs. Brown coached Doug Baldwin, Golden Tate, Jermaine Kearse and Sidney Rice and was beloved by his players and fellow staff. "He was a great friend to everybody, because he had such a positive, good, fun-loving spirit," former Seahawks head coach Pete Carroll told the team's website. "Everybody loved being around Kip. And he had a light about him, he wanted to have a good time and have fun and make things pleasant for everyone around him. That's why so many people have rallied around him in this last month or so and reached out to (his wife) Deon, being supportive and loving. He was a wonderful person, and my heart goes out to Deon and the family. It's a beautiful family." Baldwin credited Brown with helping him become the man he is today. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP "Kippy was the perfect person for us, for our group of guys who came in at that time—myself, Ricardo (Lockette), Jermaine, Golden, Sid," Baldwin told the Seahawks website. "Kippy and Sidney Rice paired really well together as being the elder statesmen in the room, helping us young guys get onboarded into the NFL life. "For me as a young person to have him as my rookie coach, I know I would not have been the player I was if it wasn't for Kippy. I owe a great deal to him as a coach who helped me develop as a player, but also the man that he was, the way that he held us accountable as young men, doing it in a way that was considerate, and we knew he was only doing it because he loved and cared about us, I wouldn't be the man that I am today without Kippy Brown." Brown is survived by his wife, Deon, and his two children, Jennifer and Jeome.

articles.title: Panthers WR Tetairoa McMillan Added 20 Pounds in Offseason, Feels 'Stronger, Faster'
articles.summary: Carolina Panthers wide receiver Tetairoa McMillan added 20 pounds during the offseason while preparing for his second year in the NFL, per Darin Gantt of the team's official website.
articles.body:
Carolina Panthers wide receiver Tetairoa McMillan added 20 pounds during the offseason while preparing for his second year in the NFL, per Darin Gantt of the team's official website.

McMillan explained that he wanted to return to his college weight.

"In college when I was heavier, I was stronger, faster," McMillan told reporters Wednesday.

49ers DE's Hilarious Plan for Australia Flight

The 23-year-old previously revealed that he ended last season at 205 pounds, via Kassidy Hill of the team's official website.

In June, McMillan confirmed that he bulked up to roughly 220 pounds.

The former Arizona standout is looking to build on his impressive rookie year, immediately establishing himself as a crucial piece of Carolina's passing attack after he was selected with the No. 8 overall pick in the 2025 NFL draft.

McMillan hauled in 70 receptions for 1,014 yards and seven touchdowns while appearing in all 17 regular-season games. He was named Offensive Rookie of the Year for his efforts.

Carolina won the NFC South and advanced to the playoffs, ultimately falling to the Los Angeles Rams in the Wild Card round. Still, McMillan caught five passes for 81 yards in his postseason debut.

The Panthers now enter their 2026 campaign looking to clinch consecutive playoff appearances for the first time since 2015.

articles.title: Ashton Jeanty's Injury Status Revealed by Raiders HC Ahead of Week 1 vs. Dolphins
articles.summary: Despite an ankle injury scare during training camp, it seems as if Las Vegas Raiders running back Ashton Jeanty will be available for the team's Sept. 13 opener against the Miami Dolphins.
articles.body:
Despite an ankle injury scare during training camp, it seems as if Las Vegas Raiders running back Ashton Jeanty will be available for the team's Sept. 13 opener against the Miami Dolphins.

"Yes," Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak told reporters Wednesday when asked if he was optimistic Jeanty would play in that contest.

While initial reporting indicated there was significant concern among the running back's teammates when he suffered the injury and was helped off the field, NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reported last month he avoided a season-ending setback.

"It's nothing like that," Rapoport said. "My understanding... is that it's an ankle sprain believed to be more low than high, and not considered to be a major injury. But it is a real injury, and the reality is, there is a chance that Ashton Jeanty may not be on the field for Week 1. They are hopeful that he will be. There is a chance that he won't be."

Kubiak's comments suggest that Jeanty will be available against the Dolphins, although ESPN's Ryan McFadden reported he didn't practice Wednesday.

Jeanty surely wants to play against a Dolphins team that may be among the Raiders' more favorable opponents of the season.

That would give him an early opportunity to build on his solid but unspectacular play from his rookie season in 2025 when he tallied 975 yards and five touchdowns on the ground behind just 3.7 yards per carry.

Las Vegas made him a franchise building block when it selected him with the No. 6 overall pick of the 2025 NFL draft, and he didn't quite live up to elevated expectations in his first year in the league.

But Jeanty now has a season of experience under his belt and will look to take a second-year leap, assuming he is healthy enough to be on the field when the regular season starts.

articles.title: George Kittle, Nick Bosa make the flight as 49ers head to Australia for historic opener: reports
articles.summary: George Kittle and Nick Bosa made the flight to Australia with the San Francisco 49ers, fueling hopes both stars will suit up against the Rams on Sept. 10.
articles.body: The San Francisco 49ers are on their way to Australia to participate in the first-ever NFL game on the continent against their NFC West foe, the Los Angeles Rams, to kick off the 2026 season. And two specific passengers have fans hopeful heading into next week’s matchup down under. Tight end George Kittle and defensive end Nick Bosa, two very important pieces of Kyle Shanahan’s roster, made the trip with the rest of the team, according to multiple reports. CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM This is encouraging considering both have been dealing with their own recovery from injury. Kittle suffered a torn Achilles in the Wild Card Round against the Philadelphia Eagles on Jan. 11, while Bosa tore his ACL in Week 3 last season. Bosa, specifically, has been battling tendinitis for most of the 49ers’ training camp. NFL COMMISSIONER ROGER GOODELL CONFIRMS LEAGUE WANTS MULTIPLE TEAMS BASED OUTSIDE THE US: 'NO DOUBT' Camp has not been at all pleasant for the 49ers in terms of depth, as multiple players have been dealing with injury, including new wide receiver Mike Evans and fullback Kyle Juszczyk on top of Kittle and Bosa. San Fran also lost wide receiver Ricky Pearsall to a PCL injury. But with Kittle and Bosa heading out to Australia, it could mean that reinforcements are on the way to start the regular season. "I would assume so," Kittle said last month when asked if traveling to Australia would indicate whether or not he’s playing in the game. "I mean, that probably makes the most sense. I would assume." After practicing on Wednesday, the 49ers took flight to Australia, where they’re expected to land on Friday due to the 17-hour time difference. It’s that time difference that the 49ers are making sure players get accustomed to it before they take on the Rams on Sept. 10 at 8:35 p.m. ET. For both teams, it will actually be Friday morning at 10:35 a.m. That’s when kickoff will take place at Melbourne Cricket Ground. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP In the days leading up to it, the availability of Kittle, Bosa and the rest of the 49ers should become clear as they hold practices and gear up for a team many believe are Super Bowl favorites this season. The Rams returned MVP quarterback Matthew Stafford, though nobody saw Aaron Donald coming out of retirement to join Myles Garrett on the defensive line after the Defensive Player of the Year was traded for with the Cleveland Browns.

articles.title: Travis Kelce health scare sparks Chiefs concern days before 2026 season opener
articles.summary: NFL News: Travis Kelce’s latest absence has put Kansas City Chiefs fans on alert just days before the team opens its 2026 campaign. The veteran tight end missed.
articles.body: Travis Kelce’s latest absence has put Kansas City Chiefs fans on alert just days before the team opens its 2026 campaign. The veteran tight end missed Kansas City’s annual kickoff luncheon on September 1 after reportedly feeling “under the weather.” While there is no indication of a serious health issue, the timing has naturally drawn attention as Kelce prepares for another demanding NFL season.Travis Kelce misses Chiefs kickoff luncheon amid health concernsThe update came through Kansas City Star reporter Pete Sweeney, who cited longtime Chiefs radio voice Mitch Holthus when reporting Kelce’s absence.“Travis Kelce is not at the Chiefs' annual kickoff luncheon. Under the weather, per Mitch Holthus,” Sweeney reported.That remains the clearest information available about Kelce’s condition. Neither the Chiefs nor the player has indicated that the illness is serious, and there has been no confirmation that it will prevent him from taking the field when Kansas City begins its season.Still, missing a major team event so close to opening day was enough to raise eyebrows.Kelce has plenty of motivation entering his 14th NFL season. The 36-year-old tight end chose to continue his career after considering retirement, and his comments during the offseason suggested that he still believes he has more to accomplish.“I've had a lot of success in the NFL, but I'm still reaching for that perfection,” Kelce told Vogue. “I still haven't played the perfect game.”His ambition has not faded with age. If anything, Kelce appears determined to make another serious run at success alongside quarterback Patrick Mahomes.“Year 14, baby, I'm fired up. Every year there's a chance to do something special, but especially coming into this year, getting Pat [Mahomes] back and wiping the slate clean.”Travis Kelce enters 2026 chasing another NFL milestoneKelce’s health update is particularly significant because he remains an important part of Kansas City’s offensive plans. Last season, he finished with 76 receptions for 851 yards. That followed a career-low 823 receiving yards in 2024, leading to questions about how much longer he can maintain his elite production.Chiefs coach Andy Reid, however, has continued to praise Kelce’s work ethic and conditioning.“You have examples like Kelce - he's the oldest guy on the team and came out every day and worked to where you had to yank him out of there to give him a breather,” Reid said.There is also history within reach.Kelce currently has 13,002 career receiving yards. He needs 45 more to move past Jason Witten and claim second place among tight ends on the NFL’s all-time receiving yardage list.For now, Kansas City has little reason to panic. Kelce was simply reported to be under the weather, with no further details released. The next few days should provide a clearer picture of whether the brief absence is nothing more than a minor setback or something the Chiefs need to monitor before kickoff.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Ravens GM says team is still waiting on NFL investigation of Rashod Bateman's arrest
articles.summary: Baltimore Ravens general manager Eric DeCosta says the team is still waiting on the NFL's investigation into receiver Rashod Bateman's arrest earlier this of...
articles.body:
OWINGS MILLS, Md. (AP) — Baltimore Ravens general manager Eric DeCosta says the team is still waiting on the NFL's investigation into receiver Rashod Bateman's arrest earlier this offseason.

"In these matters we just really kind of sit back and wait for the league and for the authorities to kind of tell us what's going on," DeCosta said. "Have no indication how long that's going to take."

Bateman was taken into custody in June in Georgia on suspicion of family violence battery and reckless conduct, both misdemeanors, and criminal damage to property, a felony.

"It's obviously something that we're very disappointed about, that we have to deal with these kind of things right now," DeCosta said. "We knew about it right away, we contacted the league right away. Spoke to the league, the league has been doing an investigation."

DeCosta spoke with reporters Wednesday, a normal occurrence shortly before the start of the season. In addition to Bateman's legal issues, he also addressed the team's kicking situation. Baltimore added Jake Moody to the practice squad this week, in effect putting starter Tyler Loop on notice after a shaky preseason.

Loop missed three of his seven field goal attempts in this year's exhibition games.

"We got to make kicks," DeCosta said. "Fresh set of legs to look at, evaluate, compare, see how it all works out. In the end, it's a performance business."

DeCosta also said he remains optimistic about working out a new contract with star quarterback Lamar Jackson. That did not happen this offseason, and the team ended up having to restructure his existing deal, which has two seasons remaining.

The biggest cause for optimism when Baltimore released its 53-man roster last weekend was the fact that defensive lineman Nnamdi Madubuike was not on injured reserve, which suggests he's expected back at some point in the first four weeks.

Madubuike missed most of last season with a neck injury.

"I'm as encouraged now as I've ever been about Nnamdi," DeCosta said. "Getting him back has been incredible."

articles.title: NFL expert urges 49ers to trade for Maxx Crosby
articles.summary: The 49ers may need to make a big trade to remain competitive in the tough NFC West.
articles.body:
The NFC West is a gauntlet heading into the 2026 NFL season, and the San Francisco 49ers may be falling behind. The Los Angeles Rams beefed up their defense with the additions of Myles Garrett and Trent McDuffie before the return of Aaron Donald, and the defending division and Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks still look dominant.

Therefore, NFL Network analyst Brian Baldinger believes the 49ers must make a swing of their own and trade for Las Vegas Raiders star edge rusher Maxx Crosby. Speaking on 95.7 The Game , Baldinger framed the trade as a necessity given what the Rams have already done on the defensive line.

"You're in an arms race with the Rams right now," Baldinger said. "This is like a military arms race trying to keep up. I don't know that Maxx Crosby is available or could be had, I have no idea. All I know is I was at the Sack Summit in Las Vegas a month ago, and nobody could beat him off the line of scrimmage. Everybody challenged him — Jared Verse, pick a guy that was out there — nobody could beat him off the ball. Nobody. He won, and they had an open competition, Maxx — I got it on video — he beat everybody off the ball."

Baldinger also dismissed concerns about the knee issue that scuttled a trade to the Baltimore Ravens back in the spring, drawing on his own playing career for context.

"I know Baltimore basically said that his knee is shot," Baldinger said. "I don't see it. I failed a physical coming in after my sixth year, failed a physical, and played six more years. They said my knee was shot. Everybody evaluates these things differently. But I feel like if you had a chance to get Maxx Crosby, he becomes your best defensive player immediately. It's infectious, the way that he plays the game, the way that he practices. Shanahan's not going to beat him in the building. On any given day, he'll beat everybody in the building. He's got the Michael Jordan mentality."

What would it cost to acquire Crosby? The Ravens traded two first-round picks, but that package seems too pricey now given what unfolded with the deal earlier this year. Bleacher Report's Alex Kay proposed a deal built around a 2027 first-rounder, a 2027 second-rounder and a 2028 third-rounder to pry Crosby loose in the wake of the Rams' Myles Garrett trade.

However, Sports Illustrated 's Albert Breer urged caution with any deal, writing that he liked the idea "in principle" but preferred San Francisco wait and see how its aging core performed before selling off draft capital. Crosby himself carries a three-year, $106.5 million extension with $91.5 million guaranteed, signed after the Baltimore deal collapsed.

The 49ers need edge rushing help, though. Nick Bosa is working back from his ACL injury and Mykell Williams is already on the physically unable to perform list and won't play for at least the first four weeks of the season. That leaves a hobbled Bosa, 2026 rookie Romello Height, Sam Okuayinonu and Keion White as the only viable pass rushers on the edge at the moment for San Francisco.

Crosby would be expensive and risky, but likely worth it to remain competitive in the division.

articles.title: Aaron Rodgers Reacts to Steelers Keeping 4 QBs in Rare Roster Move for 1st Time in Veteran's Career
articles.summary: Aaron Rodgers reacted to the Pittsburgh Steelers keeping four quarterbacks on the team's 53-man roster heading into the 2026 season.
articles.body:
Aaron Rodgers reacted to the Pittsburgh Steelers keeping four quarterbacks on the team's 53-man roster heading into the 2026 season.

"I was thinking it was a possibility, but I don't think I've been on a roster with four quarterbacks," Rodgers said Wednesday, per ESPN's Brooke Pryor .

"Obviously when you do that, you're taking away a spot from another place in the team," he added. "But at the same time, if the best 53 are going to make it -- and not saying they did -- I think those four are part of the best 53."

Rodgers will be on an active roster that contains four signal-callers for the first time in his career. Pittsburgh's quarterback room includes Mason Rudolph, Drew Allar and Will Howard.

Rudolph has spent five seasons with the Steelers while primarily operating in a reserve role. Pittsburgh selected Howard with a sixth-round pick in the 2025 NFL draft before adding Allar with a third-round pick in the 2026 draft.

"I'm happy for all those guys," Rodgers said, per Pryor. "Obviously looking to the future, those other three guys are going to have a chance when I'm done. And with the growth you saw with Will and obviously with Drew being drafted so far, but also playing well in camp, I'm not surprised at all and I'm excited about those guys' future."

The 42-year-old is the unquestioned starter in Pittsburgh and has appeared in 33 of a possible 34 regular-season games over the past two years, but it's worth noting that he previously suffered a torn Achilles in Week 1 of his 2023 campaign.

If Rodgers misses time in 2026, Rudolph is the only backup quarterback with regular-season experience on his résumé. Still, the Steelers weren't interested in parting ways with Howard or Allar after recently drafting them.

Pittsburgh will open its 2026 season against the Atlanta Falcons on Sept. 13.

articles.title: Emmitt Smith accused of conning Native American investor out of $2.5M in solar farm deal
articles.summary: Emmitt Smith and othersare accused of conning a Native American investor out of $2.5 million in an alleged solar farm scheme described as a "Ponzi scheme."
articles.body: Emmitt Smith, the Pro Football Hall of Fame running back, has been accused of conning a Native American investor out of $2.5 million, a lawsuit filed in Delaware on Monday read. The lawsuit states that Kituwah LLC, an investment and economic development sector of the Band of Cherokee Indians, loaned $2.5 million after being convinced to join an alleged solar project by Smith, his business partner David Mosley, and 413 Solutions, Inc. – their real estate company, per Front Office Sports. Kituwah claims that it has not seen "a penny" from the loan, which is more than two years past due. It also alleged that their money loaned was used to pay back a separate company that previously invested in the project. CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM Project Exodus solar farm was the name of the venture that Kituwah invested in with the understanding it would be named a partner. It alleged the U.S. Department of Energy would be funding the project as well. Kituwah LLC is seeking at least $2.5 million in damages as well as interest, costs, expenses, and anything else determined during a trial. FORMER COLLEGE BASKETBALL GUARD KERR KRIISA INDICTED IN ALLEGED $2.2M WIRE FRAUD SCHEME "Kituwah poured substantial time, efforts, and resources in the purported joint venture," the suit states. "Not only has Kituwah not seen any returns on its investment, Kituwah has been forced to expend additional costs in efforts to reclaim the amounts it is still owed pursuant to its investment, including to investigate what happened to its money." Kituwah went as far as to say it was "essentially, like a Ponzi scheme," claiming that "false projections and data" were given to them as they made the loan. They also claim that the loan was supposed to be paid back "in a matter of months." Kituwah said it did an investigation, finding that the money went to Wilson Holdings, which Smith and the other defendants in the lawsuit have partnered with on separate investments. Smith is the NFL’s all-time leading rusher, tallying 18,355 yards on the ground during his Hall of Fame career, which mostly was spent with the Dallas Cowboys. Smith won three Super Bowls with the franchise across 13 seasons, while playing his final two seasons with the Arizona Cardinals. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Smith also owns the all-time league rushing touchdowns record (164) and rushing first down record (1,028).

articles.title: Lamar Jackson Sends Warning to NFL Defenses with Bold Quote Ahead of Ravens Season
articles.summary: If Baltimore Ravens fans weren't ready for the 2026 season yet, they will be after hearing what Lamar Jackson had to say about the team's new offense.
articles.body:
If Baltimore Ravens fans weren't ready for the 2026 season yet, they will be after hearing what Lamar Jackson had to say about the team's new offense.

"I don't believe a defense is prepared for what's in store for them," he said during an interview with Adam Schein of SiriusXM.

He also said "it's making everyone's job a lot easier, and I just can't wait to showcase it."

49ers DE's Hilarious Plan for Australia Flight

Baltimore's coaching staff will look different after 18 years of John Harbaugh. It hired Jesse Minter as his replacement and then tabbed Declan Doyle as the offensive coordinator, which was an important hire since the new head coach has a defensive background.

Doyle is just 30 years old, but he impressed last season as the offensive coordinator for a Chicago Bears team that won the NFC North and reached the Divisional Round of the playoffs.

Chicago was last in the league in offensive yards in 2024 and jumped up to sixth in Doyle's first and only year with the team.

While Caleb Williams made a second-year leap while working with Doyle, Jackson is already a well-established star with two MVPs, three First-Team All-Pro selections and four Pro Bowl nods on his resume.

There isn't much else left he has to prove, although he is still chasing an elusive Super Bowl title.

With Derrick Henry, Mark Andrews, Zay Flowers and others surrounding him in the offense, perhaps this will be the season he breaks through and lifts the Lombardi Trophy. If the offense is as dangerous as Jackson made it sound during his latest comments, that is not an unrealistic scenario.

articles.title: 'I mean, clearly,' Jalen Hurts tells GQ when asked if he and A.J. Brown grew apart in Philadelphia
articles.summary: Jalen Hurts confirmed to GQ that he and A.J. Brown "clearly" grew apart before the wide receiver was traded to the New England Patriots in June.
articles.body: After an uneven 2025 season for Jalen Hurts, A.J. Brown and the Eagles’ offense as a whole, Philadelphia traded Brown to the Patriots for a pair of future draft picks. The blockbuster move came amid signs that Hurts’ once-close friendship between the franchise quarterback and star receiver had deteriorated. While more than two months have passed since Brown's move to New England, questions about his relationship with Hurts have lingered. During the Patriots’ recent joint practices with the Eagles, Brown offered a one-word response when asked whether he had spoken with Hurts since the trade. "No," Brown told reporters. While Hurts has largely avoided discussing the state of his relationship with Brown, he took a different approach this week during a sit-down interview with GQ. "There's no surprise that it was talked about," Hurts told the magazine when asked whether he and Brown had remained close, acknowledging the shift in the relationship. Hurts, the MVP of Super Bowl LIX, then effectively confirmed Brown's comments from last month, saying, "I mean, clearly," Hurts noted. In June, Brown said no single incident had sparked the rift between the two former Eagles teammates. "Nothing happened, people just grow apart. Nothing happened between me and him, or ‌our families, ⁠wives, anything. Nothing like that ever happened," Brown said at the time during an appearance on the "7PM in Brooklyn with Carmelo Anthony" podcast. AJ BROWN SAYS THERE'S BEEN SILENCE BETWEEN HIM AND EX-TEAMMATE JALEN HURTS SINCE HIS MOVE TO NEW ENGLAND "Life happens, and you just look up sometimes and you just, you find yourself drifting away, and that's fine. And I think both parties accepted that." Brown and Hurts were seen catching up together during the second of the two Patriots-Eagles joint practices in Foxborough, Massachusetts. "Honestly, guys, none of that stuff even matters, man. You all should want to report something positive. You know asking the question is going to turn negative," Brown said last month when reporters pressed him with follow-up questions about his relationship with Hurts. "So let's not get into that. Let's keep everything positive. It's love my way." Meanwhile, Hurts offered a similarly warm assessment of Brown. "I've got a lot of love for him and always have," Hurts said. Brown owns the two highest single-season receiving yardage totals in Eagles history: 1,496 yards in 2022 and 1,456 in 2023. The Eagles won the franchise’s second Vince Lombardi Trophy the following season, despite some drama involving Brown. ROB GRONKOWSKI CALLS AJ BROWN THE 'X FACTOR' TO PUT PATRIOTS BACK IN SUPER BOWL CONTENTION Philadelphia was eliminated in the wild-card round this past January, losing at home to the San Francisco 49ers. Brown then told the Eagles' front office he wanted a change of scenery, general manager Howie Roseman said at the time. Sources told ESPN that part of Brown's frustration centered on Hurts and a belief that he was not being targeted enough when he faced zone coverage. Brown also made several social media comments and comments during media sessions during the 2025 season that appeared to reflect frustration with his role in the offense. While Brown expressed gratitude for his time in the City of Brotherly Love, he said he's turned his attention to a new season with a new team. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP "It's love. I won a Super Bowl ring with them. It will always be love no matter how anyone feels. I love Philly and I will always love Philly, but I'm here now," said Brown. "That's where my feet are and that's what I'm focused on." Long before they became Eagles teammates, Hurts hosted Brown on a recruiting visit to Alabama. Their friendship deepened through offseason workouts, and Hurts eventually became godfather to Brown’s daughter, Jersee. The Eagles open the regular season Sept. 13 at home against the Washington Commanders. The Patriots, meanwhile, visit the reigning Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks on Sept. 9 for their 2026 season opener.

articles.title: Philadelphia man charged for attempted break-in at Eagles star Saquon Barkley's home in July
articles.summary: While people were home at the time of the attempted break-in, Saquon Barkley said that nobody was hurt during the incident.
articles.body:
A Philadelphia man has been arrested and charged with multiple felonies after an attempted break-in at the home of Eagles star Saquon Barkley earlier this summer.

Jabir Parker, 24, was arrested Tuesday and is facing charges related to two break-ins and the attempted break-in of a third home in the Philadelphia area this summer, according to NBC10 .

The first two break-ins, per the report, were successful. Parker allegedly broke into a home on June 22 and stole roughly $107,000 worth of jewelry. A few weeks later, Parker allegedly stole more than $687,000 worth of jewelry from a second home.

The third attempt, on July 18, was the one at Barkley's home. While officials did not name the owners of the home involved, NBC10 reported that it is owned by Barkley and his family.

"In the third burglary, the … homeowners were awakened by suspicious sounds before finding an unknown male inside the home and calling 911," the district attorney said.

Barkley told NBC10 that nobody inside the home was hurt. He has since taken up extra security.

Parker is facing multiple felonies, including burglary and conspiracy to burglary. He is still in custody as of Wednesday afternoon, and is due in court on Sept. 10.

Dallas Cowboys wide receiver CeeDee Lamb had more than $300,000 worth of luxury bags stolen from his Texas home during training camp, according to police. Both Cleveland Browns quarterback Shedeur Sanders and Tennessee titans lineman Jeffery Simmons had their homes broken into during the 2025 season, and seven individuals were charged in February for allegedly burglarizing the homes of Chiefs stars Patrick Mahomes and Travis Kelce, among others.

Barkley ran for 1,140 yards and had nine total touchdowns last season, his second with the Eagles after helping them to their Super Bowl win the year before. The Eagles will open the season against the Washington Commanders on Sept. 13.

articles.title: Alphonso Smith Jr. cause of death: How did the former Broncos cornerback die at 40?

The reports cited sources with direct knowledge of the situation. Smith was 40. His death came shortly after he posted a lengthy message on Facebook. The former cornerback opened up about serious personal struggles and described trying to fight what he called “demons.” He also spoke about painful experiences from his childhood and reflected on how those experiences had affected him.“Do not cry for me! I tried everything in my power to fight the demons behind the ones that someone put into ME!” Smith wrote in his final Facebook post.The message became even more concerning as Smith continued. He apologized to his children, family, friends and others he believed he had hurt. He also indicated that he had tried to get help.“I did not want to be that WAY! I know I have disappointed so many folks. This is a DEMON in me! But not only me! It’s EVERYONE! I have HURT so many! I needed help & did not get it,” Smith wrote on Facebook.He ended the post with another apology and the words, “I am SORRY! THIS IS IT!”The message has since become a major part of the coverage surrounding his death. Still, the circumstances of his final moments remain private, and reports have offered only limited details about what happened in Florida.Alphonso Smith Jr. made his name with Wake Forest before reaching the NFLSmith’s football story started at Wake Forest, where he developed into one of the ACC’s top defensive backs. He finished his college career with 21 interceptions, a Wake Forest record and an ACC mark at the time.The Denver Broncos selected Smith No. 37 overall in the second round of the 2009 NFL Draft. He played 15 games during his rookie season before Denver traded him to the Detroit Lions in September 2010.The move gave Smith his best NFL opportunity. In 2010, he started 10 games for Detroit and recorded a team-high five interceptions. He also returned one interception for a touchdown and finished the season with 39 tackles.Smith remained with the Lions through the 2012 season. Across four NFL seasons from 2009 through 2012, he played 42 games and finished with 88 tackles and eight interceptions.His NFL career ended in 2012, but his accomplishments at Wake Forest and his time with Denver and Detroit remain part of his football legacy. articles.title: 49ers Down Under: ABC7 Eyewitness News heads to Melbourne for Niner's season opener against Rams
articles.summary: The San Francisco 49ers are heading Down Under to open their NFL season against the Los Angeles Rams in Melbourne, and ABC7 Eyewitness News will have complet...
articles.body:
The San Francisco 49ers are heading Down Under to open their NFL season against the Los Angeles Rams in Melbourne, and ABC7 Eyewitness News will have complete coverage from Australia and the Bay Area.

ABC7's J.R. Stone will have live reports from Melbourne in the lead-up to the season opener and the latest on how 49ers fans are enjoying everything Australia has to offer.

The Niners will leave Wednesday night from California, arrive in Melbourne Friday morning, and then take time to adjust to the new time zone. They will hold a light practice on Saturday, take Sunday off and then have a normal stretch of three practices on Monday through Wednesday before playing the opener on Friday morning.

They will leave right after the game and are expected to land back in the Bay Area on Friday afternoon. They then will be able to take the weekend off before preparing for the Week 2 game against Miami on Sept. 20.

"It's a big adjustment on the body," coach Kyle Shanahan said. "So, the recommendation for everybody has been to tell us when to go, and it's made a lot of sense. I know how our players feel also. I was a little bit on the fence. Science wasn't and what I was reported on and our players weren't at all. So that helped me get off the fence."

The Rams consulted with their own scientists and came up with the opposite approach. They will do most of their practice at home and aren't expected to arrive in Australia until about 24 hours before the game, hoping the short stay leads to no jet lag.

The better option might not be known until after the game.

The approach by the Niners has made the past few days a whirlwind. The players got the weekend off after playing the final exhibition game on Thursday night in Las Vegas and resumed practice on Monday - the day after the roster was reduced to 53 players.

The front office had to make those cuts, put together a practice squad and figure out which players would be healthy for Week 1 to make sure they had the correct roster in place before departing.

"There's a lot behind the scenes," general manager John Lynch said. "Our logistics folks, our folks that work in the cafe, have just gone to tremendous lengths, our health and performance team, to make sure that we're giving our players the best opportunity to feel right when they play down there in Australia. Everything from getting visas, which much more complicated than I ever knew, and they've been outstanding. ... Hats off to those guys for pulling off a monumental task, and it's not done yet."

Lynch said he had to make sure all the practice squad players he wanted to sign had passports with one needing his parents to send it overnight. It was an even bigger scramble for offensive lineman Jarrett Patterson, who was acquired in a trade from Houston on Sunday.

"They were like, hey, do you have a passport? We're leaving for Australia in three days," he said. "I was like, 'Whoa!' It's obviously a quick turnaround getting here a couple hours after I found out and now getting ready for Australia."

But in all, the players are welcoming the challenge and opportunity. Cornerback Deommodore Lenoir said he'd travel 30 hours if needed to play in an NFL game and rookie De'Zhaun Stribling has a must-see item on his to-do list before making his debut.

"I kind of want to see a kangaroo, just because," he said. "To see how big they are."

The opener against the Rams will have an additional challenge after the Rams brought Aaron Donald out of retirement to join Myles Garrett on one of the fiercest defensive lines in the game.

Donald is a three-time AP Defensive Player of the Year but was out of football the past two seasons. His 12 1/2 career sacks against the 49ers in the regular season and playoffs are tied with Kevin Greene for the most ever.

"They got better, certainly, with him deciding to come out of retirement," Lynch said. "Now, there's time away. But I know that guy trains like a madman. I ran into him in a hotel somewhere a while back and we had some fun chatter back and forth. Never thought he'd do it. But he's doing it and so we better get ready for it."

If you are heading to Melbourne to watch the 49ers, share your experience with ABC7 Eyewitness News!

The Associated Press contributed to this article.

articles.title: NFL QB pressure index 2026: Joe Burrow, Justin Herbert among QBs with most to prove
articles.summary: Being an NFL quarterback means constant pressure to perform -- but these 9 passers have a bit more riding on the 2026 season.
articles.body:
Being an NFL quarterback means constant pressure to succeed.

Every game, from Week 1 onward, will be used as data by fans to measure how good a passer and their team is. With a few bad outings, injury issues, or a failure to live up to high expectations, in the blink of an eye, a starter may become a backup — there are only 32 QB1 spots to go around.

A case can be made that every NFL quarterback has some kind of pressure to succeed in the 2026 season. Even Sam Darnold, fresh off a Super Bowl victory, may be out to prove his 2025 was no fluke. But some quarterbacks have more riding on the upcoming season than others.

Here's a ranking of the nine quarterbacks facing the most pressure to succeed in 2026.

Tina MacIntyre-Yee/Democrat and Chronicle / USA TODAY NETWORK via Imagn Images

Josh Allen turned 30 years old in May. He's tracking to be one of the greatest quarterbacks of all-time, one of the biggest stars of his era and should have plenty more elite years left in the tank. However, with every year he doesn't reach a Super Bowl, the Bills have more questions to answer — and it already reached a tipping point this offseason.

Sean McDermott, the only coach Allen had ever played for in Buffalo, was fired after yet another heartbreaking playoff loss, the seventh consecutive season in which the Bills made the playoffs with at least 10 wins but failed to reach the Super Bowl. And this time, Patrick Mahomes and the Chiefs weren't even to blame.

Even with Kansas City taking a step back in 2025, Buffalo couldn't emerge from the AFC. Yet, at this point, there's still almost an expectation that come every January, the Bills will be in the playoffs thanks to Allen's talents.

Here's their regular season record and playoff result in every season since Allen took over in 2018:

2019: 10-6 (lost to Texans in wild card)

2020: 13-3 (lost to Chiefs in AFC Championship)

2021: 11-6 (lost to Chiefs in divisional round)

2022: 13-3 (lost to Bengals in divisional round)

2023: 11-6 (lost to Chiefs in divisional round)

2024: 13-4 (lost to Chiefs in AFC Championship)

2025: 12-5 (lost to Broncos in divisional round)

The Bills have lived and died by Allen's performances for years, whether that's fair or not. It's the way their offense is designed and how they have won so many games. With Joe Brady taking over as head coach, there may not be anybody else to blame if the Bills can't make a Super Bowl push in 2026.

There's no chance the Bills move on from Allen next offseason, even in a worst-case scenario, but he's only going to be a Super Bowl-level quarterback for so long. With every missed opportunity in Buffalo, Allen's career trajectory looks more like Dan Marino.

Put Joe Burrow in the same category as Allen. They're both veteran star quarterbacks who have consistently come up short of a ring, primarily because of Mahomes' Chiefs, who also failed to step up in the AFC last year despite Kansas City's struggles. There are two key differences with Burrow: he has been to a Super Bowl, and he's set to hit free agency a year before Allen, in 2030.

That year of difference in contract length — especially with Cincinnati missing the playoffs in three straight years — means the results of 2026 could wind up dictating Burrow's long-term future with the team. Partly due to his injury issues, the Bengals haven't been an AFC contender since their 2022 loss to the Chiefs in the AFC Championship Game.

Here's how the Bengals have performed since Burrow took over as quarterback in 2020:

2022: 12-4 (lost to Chiefs in AFC Championship Game)

For a quarterback of Burrow's caliber, four missed playoffs in six years won't cut it. With every disappointment in Cincinnati, pressure mounts on them to succeed before there's a threat of Burrow departing while still in his prime.

It's not yet a realistic threat to consider the Bengals needing to move on from Burrow. But if you picture the end of the 2026 season, if the team misses the playoffs again, that may become a question it has to answer sooner than expected. That also puts pressure on Burrow to not just stay healthy, but prove he's still capable of the heights he's reached in 2021 and 2022.

Through three NFL seasons, C.J. Stroud's best was his first, when he threw for over 4,000 yards and 23 touchdowns as he became a star for the Texans . Since then, he simply has not been great enough for Houston's offense to be a Super Bowl threat.

By now, it's clear that the Texans have the defensive talent to contend for a title; that side of the ball was the backbone of their 12-win season in 2025. If Stroud can distribute the ball at the elite rate he was in 2023, there's a chance that the Texans make national noise.

The Texans are a good team with Stroud leading the way. That much is clear. The question is whether they can be a great team, something that can only happen with the best version of their quarterback.

There's also an intriguing contract angle to Stroud's 2026 season — he has yet to come to terms on a rookie extension with Houston, carrying a club option for 2027 before 2028 free agency. With a bad season for the Texans, perhaps they're unwilling to sign Stroud to a contract that compares to his peers.

If Stroud can't uplift Houston's offense this season, he's another big name whose future could be up in the air.

There may be no more obvious quarterback facing pressure in their career this NFL season than Tua Tagovailoa. The Dolphins accepted a record-setting $99.2 million total dead cap just to release him this offseason, which isn't exactly a vote of confidence in his abilities. Add in his concussion/injury history and a preseason competition with Michael Penix Jr., and Tagovailoa has had a bit of a fall from grace.

Even with Penix not playing throughout training camp, Atlanta has been unwilling to name Tagovailoa as its starter. Just two seasons ago, he led the NFL in passing yards. But already, with one more rough stretch, Tagovailoa could be staring down becoming a rest-of-career backup.

In the best-case scenario, Tagovailoa can maximize the Falcons ' offensive weapons and Kevin Stefanski's play calling, holding onto the starting quarterback job and setting himself for a longer-term deal next offseason. Anything other than that, though, will make his NFL future far murkier.

Any quarterback who needs a competition to win the starting job faces pressure. But Tagovailoa's injury history and historic release from the Dolphins make him even more of a make-or-break candidate for 2026.

To this point, the Buccaneers have been unable to come to an extension agreement with Baker Mayfield, who has led the team since 2023. His time in Tampa Bay has included two playoff trips but just one 10-plus-win season, and while Mayfield has put up strong numbers, the Buccaneers have been unable to become a true NFC threat.

Tampa Bay seems to have a high floor every year, with the offensive talent to compete with virtually any opponent. But the team needs Mayfield at his best to contend for the NFC South title, and as he enters Year 9 of his up-and-down career, the quarterback hasn't proven he can go on a deep playoff run.

Mayfield's contract situation is perhaps the most intriguing of any NFL starting quarterback. If he can't lead the Buccaneers to the playoffs this fall, he may be on a new team in 2027.

Another AFC quarterback who hasn't been able to overcome Mahomes' shadow? Justin Herbert. The Chargers QB has regularly made his club good — like Stroud or Mayfield with their teams — but it's still unclear if he can lead a team to the promised land.

Herbert typically doesn't receive much blame for the Chargers' inability to break through, because for the most part, he's been consistently great despite issues surrounding him, whether on the offensive line or defensively. But at some point, the NFL is always about quarterback play.

Regardless of an injury to center Tyler Biadasz, there's a clear path for the Chargers to be the AFC West's best team in 2026. Unlike counterparts like Allen or Burrow, however, Herbert hasn't been able to lead L.A. even past the wild-card round. If that happens again, it could lead to more significant changes for the franchise, even if Herbert is around for the long-term.

The final AFC quarterback on this list, Lamar Jackson, is one who has individually dominated every NFL season, but also hasn't put it all together for a Super Bowl run.

There are no longer any questions about Jackson's capabilities as a passer, and we've known for years he can run with the best offensive weapons in the NFL. But with one conference championship appearance to Jackson's name and a missed playoff trip in 2025, John Harbaugh was let go, shifting some of the focus to the Ravens ' star quarterback to prove that was the right decision.

The reason Jackson ranks lower than Allen or Burrow here, however, is partially due to the fact that Jackson can't be fully blamed for Baltimore's 2025 struggles, throwing for 21 touchdowns and seven interceptions. There's a clear overall trend of his individual excellence every year despite the team coming up short.

The pressure in Baltimore for 2026 is more on Jessie Minter and the Ravens' defense than Jackson and the offense. But as noted with other quarterbacks, at the end of the day, the players at that position are expected to lead their team regardless of circumstances. Jackson still hasn't reached the biggest stage in football despite his electric play.

Another Eagles season, another new playcaller for Jalen Hurts. With a Super Bowl ring to his name, Hurts deserves more leeway than most NFL quarterbacks, but with Philadelphia's offense struggling in 2025, he needs to prove that was due to the playcalling and not his limitations on the field.

Everywhere Hurts has gone, he's been a winner. He hasn't missed the playoffs yet as an NFL starter. But merely making the dance is no longer the expectation for Hurts — once he proved he could lead Philadelphia to the Super Bowl, Eagles fans' appetites changed. Anything but NFC East crowns and deep playoff runs is considered a disappointment, which is a high, but fair bar to set.

Hurts' 2025 numbers (11-5 record, 25 touchdowns, six interceptions) don't indicate he needs much of a bounce-back season, but there needs to be offensive improvement in Philadelphia with Sean Marrion at offensive coordinator and A.J. Brown gone. If Hurts can't answer the doubters this time, with just two years remaining on his deal after 2026, his future in the City of Brotherly Love could look a bit different.

John Jones - IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect

Rounding out the list is a quarterback in a very similar situation to Tagovailoa, but with a better track record and system around him: Kyler Murray. The Cardinals made the expensive decision to let him go this offseason, and while Murray has flashed plenty of elite arm talent and dual-threat capabilities, it hasn't led to any kind of team success in the NFL.

Murray, hypothetically, now has everything he needs to succeed: an offensive-minded head coach, some elite weapons around him, a QB1 job and a winning culture in Minnesota. It's clear that he has the talent to succeed, but his motivation has been called into question. In a contract year, those are questions that need to be answered.

Murray is playing on a one-year deal with the Vikings, making this a make-or-break year for him. His talent would still likely give him more future opportunities, but no team is going to be willing to sign him to a significant contract in free agency next spring if he can't keep Minnesota competitive.
